items.title: 68436_Alberta Hunter oral history interview
items.q: No, D.C. didn't want no show business for Lil.

ctx.x: D.C. wasn't -- you met D.C. didn't you?

No, D.C. didn't want no show business for Lil. Uh-uh. But my mother was a different type person. My mother -- she didn't criticize show business. And she didn't try to keep me out of show business. As long as I was a good girl, she always told me, be a lady. Always be a lady. That was beaten in my head all my life. Respect yourself, and you'll be respected. That was always my training, see. And so my mother, when my mother came to Chicago -- came to Memphis -- I mean, came from Memphis to Chicago, she contented…
people. Never visited anybody. She stayed in the house by herself. But she had everything that a poor girl could give her mother, because I saw to that, you know.
